t: Patients with executive impairment showed higher total motor score, HY stage, depression, fatigue, and total dysautonomia than those without executive impairment.
Age and cardiac remodeling jointly were associated with an advanced circadian acrophase in the SNS Index, SDNN, and RMSSD, and a delayed phase in pNN50 among older CR patients.

During head-up tilt, patients with CSS showed higher heart rate, systolic/mean/diastolic blood pressure, and respiratory frequency, lower end-tidal CO2, and greater decline in cerebral blood flow velocity compared with patients without CSS.
All three clinical groups (LC+, LC−, POTS) showed significantly higher anxiety symptomatology than healthy controls, with POTS patients scoring higher than controls.
Patients with visuospatial impairment showed higher total motor score, HY stage, depression, and total dysautonomia than those without visuospatial impairment.
New or worsening pain conditions after COVID were reported by 94.4% of Long COVID patients versus 0% of controls.
Dysautonomia (postural hypotension, constipation, urge incontinence) was significantly more frequent in PD patients who fell at least once versus non-fallers in bivariate analysis.
ME/CFS participants with COMPASS-31 pupillomotor risk had significantly greater pain, cognitive impairment, fatigue, and reduced general/physical functioning than those without pupillomotor risk.
Patients with memory impairment had higher total motor symptom scores and HY stage than those without.

fESC values differed significantly across systolic BP scoring subgroups, with the lowest values in patients with the most severe orthostatic intolerance (BP score 2) compared to those without hypotension (BP score 0).

Reinfection was associated with significantly increased risk of a range of other PASC-related symptoms and conditions spanning cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, neurological, dermatological, and respiratory systems, including myocarditis, thrombophlebitis and thromboembolism, heart disease, acute kidney injury, fluid and electrolyte disturbance, arrhythmias, abnormal liver enzymes, cognitive impairment, fatigue and malaise, mental ill health, and changes in taste and smell.

Among the 24 PASC-related symptoms and conditions assessed, reinfected children and adolescents had a significantly increased risk of POTS or dysautonomia compared with those with only a first infection, as part of a broader range of elevated risks (RR range 1.15-3.60 across all 24 outcomes).

In adjusted quantile regression models, BMI remained independently associated with heart rate dynamics (negatively with mean RR, positively with mean HR), while physical activity group lost significance for these parameters after adjustment.

Age, female sex, diabetes, obesity, smoking, chronic kidney disease, history of stroke, and peripheral artery disease were identified as independent clinical determinants that negatively affect HRR60 in a multivariate regression model.

Neutrophil count, lymphocyte count, platelet count, NLR, PLR, LMR, SII, and hs-CRP differed significantly among T2D patients with normal carotid arteries, carotid intima-media thickening, and carotid plaque.

In MSA, smaller right vagus nerve CSA correlated inversely with higher LF/HF ratio and LFnu of systolic/diastolic blood pressure variability across resting, upright, and supine positions, suggesting a link between vagal atrophy and sympathetic predominance in blood pressure regulation.

Participants with reflex (vasovagal) syncope had significantly higher total COMPASS 31 scores and orthostatic intolerance, vasomotor, gastrointestinal, and bladder domain scores than healthy controls.

Four distinct radiographic patterns of thalamic infarction have been described on diffusion-weighted MRI, with bilateral paramedian thalamic infarction with mesencephalic involvement being the most common (43%), as seen in this patient.
In FD patients, Δmean LF/HF and Δmean HF did not differ significantly between sleep and awake periods, indicating loss of the normal circadian rhythm of ANS activity.

Vitamin D deficiency (vs normal levels) was significantly associated with lower time- and frequency-domain HRV indices, including SDNN, SDANN, LF, and LF/HF ratio, after adjustment for cardiovascular and diabetic risk factors.
Patients with language impairment had higher total motor symptom scores and HY stage than those without, but no significant differences in depression, anxiety, fatigue, or total dysautonomia.

Lying, seated, and standing resting heart rates were all significantly lower in the chronotropic incompetence group and the chronotropic-medication group compared to the non-chronotropic-incompetence group.

On multivariable regression, baseline supine SBP level, supine SBP decline, and white-coat effect were all significant negative independent predictors of the orthostatic SBP response, while alcohol intake was a significant positive independent predictor.

In a multivariable model adjusted for age, HbA1c, BMI, eGFR and diabetes duration, higher neopterin remained independently associated with cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy, with each 1-SD increase associated with a 2.67-fold higher odds of CAN and each 1 nmol/L increase associated with a 1.32-fold higher odds.

Fisher's z tests showed that racial differences in HRV-catecholamine correlations were significant only among males: Black males showed significantly stronger correlations than White males for HR-epinephrine, LF-HRV-norepinephrine, and HF-HRV-norepinephrine.

In adjusted quantile regression models, physical activity group remained significantly and independently associated with LF power, whereas HF power and LF/HF ratio were not significantly associated with activity group after adjustment.

Survivors showed the expected reduction in HRV with rising blood CO2 (hypercapnia), whereas non-survivors showed a paradoxical positive correlation between HRV and CO2, indicating dissociation of physiologic autonomic adaptation to respiratory failure in fatal cases.
Females with cardiac remodeling exhibited lower AmpEN MESOR, amplitude, and an advanced phase, while sex alone (independent of remodeling) predicted higher SampEN MESOR in females.
The magnitude of CTRA gene expression decline was significantly greater in participants who had experienced more SARS-CoV-2 infection events prior to study entry.

Non-survivors had elevated serum BNP, left atrial size, interventricular septal and posterior wall thickness (all p<0.01), and left ventricular end-systolic volume (p=0.022) compared with survivors, suggesting subclinical cardiac sarcoid involvement predicts mortality.
In the low LF/HF (parasympathetic-predominant) subgroup, both LLLA and EA significantly improved LF%, HF%, LF/HF ratio, total HRV, and SDNN compared with sham LLLA, with reversed changes in RMSSD.
Low-dose propranolol significantly reduced both lying (102.7 to 81.6 bpm) and standing (132.1 to 101.0 bpm) heart rates in children with inappropriate sinus tachycardia.
Ivabradine significantly reduced both lying (103.3 to 84.2 bpm) and standing (128.6 to 105.4 bpm) heart rates in children with inappropriate sinus tachycardia.
Omega-3 fatty acid supplementation significantly reduced both lying (96.4 to 88.6 bpm) and standing (121.5 to 112.1 bpm) heart rates in children with inappropriate sinus tachycardia.
OH was independently associated with a higher prevalence of at least one comorbidity, even after adjusting for supine and seated hypertension status.

In a single AAG patient treated with intravenous immunoglobulins, pupillary fatigue mildly improved after treatment (redilation started at 0.74 s post-treatment vs 0.97 s pre-treatment), while parasympathetic impairment and apraclonidine response were unchanged.

A gradient-boosted machine learning model distinguished participants with vs without ocular symptoms with an AUC of 0.77, identifying dizziness, cold intolerance, pressure at base of head, tinnitus, and tremors as the top differentiating symptoms.

Bivariate correlations showed that greater decline in estimated failure load was associated with greater deterioration in total vBMD, cortical area, cortical vBMD, and cortical thickness, while a greater increase in trabecular area was associated with decline in estimated failure load.
Short-term LLTS treatment did not significantly change antibody ELISA levels or functional receptor-activating activity for either α1AR or β1AR autoantibodies.

Responders to HBOT (≥10-point SF-36 PF improvement) showed larger reductions in thalamic sensorimotor connectivity from pre- to post-treatment than non-responders, whose reductions were limited to small clusters.

Baseline heart rate, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure did not differ significantly as a group between the July 2021 and February 2022 test sessions, despite individual variability.

Mean cerebral blood flow velocity (CBFv) fell by an average of 27.7% (range 14.1–36%) during needle-induced syncope, accompanied by widening of the systolic-diastolic CBFv difference (baseline 62.7 cm/s vs syncope 95.8 cm/s), indicating active cerebral arteriolar vasodilation.
During needle-induced syncope all patients showed a bradycardic response, with heart rate reductions averaging 29 bpm (range 15.6–51.1 bpm).
Needle-induced syncope was accompanied by marked hypotension, with mean blood pressure reductions averaging 54.2% (range 44.3–69.5%).

Lower NDI in left cingulum, forceps minor, left IFOF, and left SLF, and higher FISO in left ATR, left corticospinal tract, left uncinate fasciculus, and right ATR were associated with more severe anxiety (HAMA-14).
Parkinson's disease patients with gastrointestinal symptoms showed significantly greater orthostatic hypotension compared to those without gastrointestinal symptoms.

SCOPA-AUT sub-scores significantly increased over 5 years of follow-up in gastrointestinal, urinary, cardiovascular, pupillomotor, thermoregulatory, and male sexual domains in PD, but not in the female sexual dysfunction domain.
Low-dose propranolol significantly reduced the standing heart rate increase in children with POTS from 42.2 ± 15.9 to 27.2 ± 17.4 bpm.
Ivabradine significantly reduced the standing heart rate increase in children with POTS from 37.5 ± 16.4 to 23.6 ± 8.12 bpm.
Omega-3 fatty acid supplementation significantly reduced the standing heart rate increase in children with POTS from 44.0 ± 11.9 to 25.6 ± 8.4 bpm.
Overall Lewy pathology positivity in the cohort was significantly associated with older age at death and with more advanced neurofibrillary tangle and senile plaque staging.
Higher (better) MoCA cognitive scores at baseline were associated with a 7% lower risk, per additional point, of transitioning from one-or-no falls to recurrent falls.

Use of antidepressants was associated with a 35% lower probability of transitioning from recurrent falls to the favourable one-or-no-falls state, and an 87% higher risk of transitioning from one-or-no-falls to recurrent falls.

In those reporting one or no falls at baseline, older age (per 5-year interval) and higher number of chronic conditions each significantly increased the risk of transitioning to the recurrent-falls state.
Post-tilt cerebral blood flow reduction increased progressively with ME/CFS disease severity, with disease severity being the strongest predictor of impaired CBF recovery in regression analysis.

In a matched comparison, MSA patients with exclusively motor symptoms (no dysautonomia) at their final visit had a significantly longer disease duration than matched patients with autonomic symptoms present.
Dysautonomia was one of the most common presenting symptoms in pediatric CASPR2 antibody-related neurological syndrome, occurring in 44.8% of the 67 patients.
Executive impairment was independently associated with higher UPDRS-III, HY stage, depression, and fatigue scores in adjusted logistic regression.

Lower-performing T1DM participants had significantly higher long-term (disease-onset-to-examination) HbA1c than higher-performing T1DM participants, though the single most recent HbA1c value did not differ.

In contrast, Lewis et al. found no significant difference in FIS scores between CFS-POTS and CFS patients without POTS, and CFS-POTS patients actually had lower total Chalder fatigue scores than CFS patients without POTS, despite greater orthostatic intolerance and autonomic dysfunction.
By 24-week follow-up, most patients had normalized bladder compliance and recovered detrusor function, with only a small minority showing persistent abnormalities.
The three best-performing ERTS definitions (SBP≥20, SBP≥15, and SBP≥20 and/or DBP≥15) showed very good agreement with each other according to weighted kappa statistics.
SYNE2, encoding nesprin-2, showed genome-wide significant rare-variant burden and is proposed to affect nuclear-cytoskeletal connections in mechanically stressed muscle tissue.

The proportion of GBS patients requiring mechanical ventilation was 13.8% of adults and 8.9% of children, lower than rates reported in some prior international studies (e.g., IGOS 19%, Thailand 50.9%).

Beta-blocker use in cardiac remodeling patients had a modest effect on select circadian HRV parameters (SDNN, pNN50, REC, ShannE, SD2 MESOR), but cardiac remodeling group effects remained significant after adjustment, indicating the chronodisruption was not solely medication-driven.
In a subgroup of 23 patients followed for at least 3 years, feet electrochemical skin conductance (fESC) values declined significantly from baseline to the 2- and 3-year evaluations.

Morphological stress assessment of fished octopuses showed that 55.2% had high vitality with light or no damage, 20.7% had low vitality with mantle bruises and one injured arm, 20.7% had midrange vitality with mantle bruises and more than one injured arm, and 3.4% (1 animal) was fished dead.

DAB2IP, genome-wide significant in the burden analysis and also nominally significant in the gene-based GWAS, is a known heart-rate-associated gene that regulates vascular endothelial apoptosis via the DAB2IP-ASK1-JNK pathway.

Safety analysis across seven studies (1292 patients) found LCIG-related gastrointestinal AEs in 8.4% of patients, urinary AEs (UTI) in 0.5%, and cardiovascular AEs (OH, atrial fibrillation, congestive cardiac failure, ventricular tachycardia) in 1.1%.

A decline in physical activity over the follow-up period showed only a borderline correlation with decline in estimated failure load, and this effect was diminished after adjusting for demographic factors.
CPAP therapy was associated with a significant decrease in SDNN, RMSSD, CV, and SD1 during wakefulness, with no significant changes during sleep.
Participants with reflex syncope had higher total COMPASS 31 scores and orthostatic intolerance, vasomotor, and gastrointestinal domain scores than participants with presyncope only.
OIR-tilt at initial assessment was significantly lower in patients who later phenoconverted from PAF than in those with stable PAF, despite no significant difference in raw ΔSBP alone.

In a sample of 128 CPETs in early PD (SPARX study), 18.8% showed chronotropic incompetence, 66.4% showed normal chronotropic response, and 14.8% showed an exaggerated chronotropic response relative to age-predicted maximal heart rate.

In vasovagal syncope patients, blood volume increased after 3-4 months of HUTS in six of eight cases, and this increase correlated with prolonged time to syncope, while two cases without increased plasma volume showed little to no improvement in orthostatic tolerance.
In patients with PCC, ST produced greater lymph node discomfort than MICT, while MICT produced greater concentration difficulty than ST.
DBPVM2l_rise significantly correlated with Valsalva baseline SBP, shorter PRT, and higher SBP overshoot, but not with resting logLFSBP or blood volume deviation.

In four illustrative subjects, the correlation between RRI and RQTdiff was strong in healthy individuals but weaker in individuals with T2DM, suggesting diabetes attenuates the coupling between these ECG measures.
Thermal dysesthesias and hyperesthesia of digital extremities were present in 45% of PASC-vac patients and were statistically more prevalent in females.
In FTD, increased overall autonomic symptoms were positively correlated with larger (not smaller) hypothalamic subregional and total volumes, contrary to the hypothesized negative correlation.
Patients with both GBA variants and high dysautonomia (SCOPA-AUT≥18) had the highest risk of anxiety progression, 7.5 times higher than iPD patients with low dysautonomia.
MDD patients had significantly older age at IH onset, lower ESS scores, more disrupted sleep, less non-refreshing naps, and less sleep inertia compared to non-MDD IH patients.
Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension did not significantly predict conversion to cognitive impairment.
Dysautonomia was significantly more common in refractory, ICU-dependent NMDARE (RI-NMDARE) patients than in the rest of the severe NMDARE cohort.

Principal component analysis using endothelial biomarkers alone correctly distinguished 51% of ME/CFS from long COVID patients, versus 35% using inflammatory biomarkers alone, and 59% using both combined.

Nocturnal polyuria and voiding dysfunction showed no significant correlation with age, disease duration, or cardiovascular autonomic parameters including orthostatic blood pressure drop, supine hypertension, deep breathing responses, Valsalva ratio, or circadian blood pressure patterns.

In a sensitivity analysis additionally adjusting for disease duration at enrollment, the subgroup (extensive vs restricted dysautonomia) effect on mortality was no longer significant, while disease duration and baseline severity emerged as independent predictors of mortality.
The number of reported long COVID symptoms significantly declined over follow-up time relative to symptom onset in a linear mixed-effects model.

Patients with nOH had more prolonged pressure recovery time, attenuated pressor and heart rate responses to isometric exercise, lower Valsalva ratio, reflecting more widespread sympathetic and parasympathetic autonomic failure.

Lower E:I ratio (greater parasympathetic dysfunction) was associated with poorer executive function (FAB) and visuospatial performance (Benson Figure Copy) and greater functional impairment (PD-CFRS) specifically in GBA-PD; Valsalva Ratio also correlated with cognitive measures.
PD patients with REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) had a higher frequency of dysautonomia than PD patients without RBD.
After adjustment for age and sex, higher neopterin remained significantly associated with greater odds of cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy.

Compared with the self-reported Big POTS survey cohort (>5500 adults), the medically confirmed LT-POTS cohort had significantly higher employment (58.9% vs 48.0%) and lower rates of job loss (6.8% vs 20.9%) and other work impacts due to POTS.
Mortality was higher among RI-NMDARE patients compared with severe non-refractory NMDARE patients.

In LOPD, high baseline C16 glucosylceramide was associated with higher unadjusted cumulative incidence of autonomic dysfunction, but this association did not persist as an independent predictor in covariate-adjusted Cox models.
Patients with sudomotor dysfunction of the feet were older, had longer diabetes duration, lower RR ratio, and greater orthostatic systolic/diastolic BP drops.

Persistent nausea and vomiting at 1 year were associated with higher risk of GI-related death and need for nutritional support; persistent diarrhea at 1 year was similarly associated with increased need for nutritional support and GI-related death.

Healthy controls showed a normal circadian ANS rhythm with significantly higher Δmean LF/HF (sympathetic) during awake vs sleep periods and higher Δmean HF (parasympathetic) during sleep vs awake periods.

Twelve newly diagnosed POTS cases (equally split between post-COVID and post-vaccination) received pharmacological treatment, including combination therapy with fludrocortisone plus a beta-blocker or ivabradine in two individuals.

Higher HRV minimum values were correlated with worse (longer) performance across multiple TUG gait sub-tasks (stand up, walk away, rotation, walk back, sit down, total time) at both comfortable and fast walking pace.

Autonomic dysfunction, particularly cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and thermoregulatory subdomains measured by SCOPA-AUT, mediated the longitudinal relationship between daytime sleepiness (ESS) and cognitive decline (MoCA) in PD patients.

In healthy controls, semiorthostatic stress (60° head elevation) produced an integrated hemodynamic response with decreased stroke volume and cardiac index, compensatory increases in heart rate and MAP, and a concomitant significant decrease in peripheral perfusion index, but this integrated response was lost in both septic and nonseptic critically ill patients.

Mean heart rate contributed significantly to CADF cluster classification and is cited as an independent predictor of reduced life expectancy, with a 10 bpm increase associated with a 30% increase in mortality in prior literature.
Backward conditional logistic regression identified discharge status, ICU admission, and absence of antecedent gastroenteritis as significant predictors of longer hospital stay.
MSA-P patients had significantly higher prevalence of musculoskeletal and connective tissue diseases than MSA-C patients.
Correlation between changes in heart rate and mean arterial pressure was significantly weaker in non-survivors than survivors of COVID-19 at early, intermediate, and late ICU timepoints.

Heart rate recovery (both fast and slow phase) was significantly better in healthy active adults compared to both the mild TBI and healthy sedentary groups, with no difference between mild TBI and sedentary groups.

ERS showed weak but statistically significant positive correlations with WBC count, haemoglobin, age, and stroke severity (GCS), but no significant correlation with CRP, sodium, potassium, or blood pressure.
AN-scores remained significantly higher in dialysis patients than controls even after dichotomizing the dialysis group by diabetes duration (above/below median of 16 years).

Patients with liver transaminases ≥3 times the upper limit of normal at admission showed a numerically higher rate of cardiovascular instability (50%) than those with levels ≤2 times ULN (26.2%), but this did not reach statistical significance.

At 3 months, the high-DC group had a substantially higher rate of favorable functional outcomes than the low-DC group, with over 85% of high-DC patients having mild or no disability compared to a more uniform, worse distribution in the low-DC group.

A 38-year-old woman with CRPS type I of the right foot had ~80% pain improvement and complete resolution of edema, flushing, erythema, mottling, and hyperpigmented skin lesions 2 weeks after percutaneous DRG stimulation trial, with sustained improvement at 1 year after permanent DRG stimulator placement.
Older cardiac remodeling patients showed a significantly lower SD2/SD1 MESOR and amplitude compared with older controls, indicating impaired long-range autonomic coordination with age and remodeling.

Autonomic symptoms including urinary incontinence, thermoregulatory dysfunction, and pupillary dysfunction showed significant yearly progression in odds of occurrence, along with an overall rise in SCOPA-AUT score, while COMPASS-31 did not change significantly.

Donors with severe orthostatic intolerance showed markedly larger drops in systolic, diastolic and mean arterial pressure, larger heart rate rise, and greater cerebral oxygenation decline on standing after blood donation compared with orthostatic-tolerant donors.
At 6 hours postoperatively in the supine position, MAP was significantly higher and its reduction smaller in OLIF versus MIS-TLIF patients.

Among adult brainstem gliomas, H3K27-altered DMG accounts for 37.2% of cases and IDH-mutant glioma for 26.5%, with IDH-mutant tumors showing markedly better overall survival (43.8 months) than DMG (11.4 months).
No differences were found between normosmic vs. abnormal, or hyposmic vs. anosmic PD participants, in baseline SCOPA-AUT total score or MDS-UPDRS III total and sub-scores.

Tilt test HR, CHEPs N latency, cognitive performance, fatigue level, sleep quality, depressive symptomatology, and anxiety symptoms best discriminated ME/CFS patients from healthy controls, with fatigue level again showing near-perfect diagnostic accuracy.

Change in orthostatic heart rate increase from admission to discharge was not significantly correlated with changes in maximum heart rate, resting respirations, trapezoid muscle tension, self-reported symptoms, or self-reported functioning.
A higher SD1/SD2 ratio on 24-hour Holter monitoring was significantly associated with mortality among sarcoidosis patients.
Patients with hives had greater duration and frequency of painful episodes, and pain was more often triggered by pressure or cold, but not by brushing.

In a cited cohort of 44 Hirayama disease patients, parasympathetic dysfunction was demonstrated via decreased expiration/inspiration ratio of heart rate, decreased 30/15 R-R interval ratio, and altered acceleration-deceleration response to standing.

In a separately cited survey of 488 people with ME/CFS (Clague-Baker et al., 2023), HR monitoring helped 72% of participants better understand their personalized PEM, with 69% citing real-time activity feedback and 64% reporting it helped stop the boom/bust or push-crash cycle.

In PD, mean total SCOPA-AUT score significantly increased from baseline to 5 years and continued to increase from 5 to 7 years, whereas no significant increase occurred in healthy controls over 5 years.
CRP levels were positively correlated with AN-scores across all patients, though this correlation narrowly missed significance when dialysis patients and controls were analyzed separately.
Higher SCOPA-AUT (autonomic dysfunction) scores were significantly associated with geriatric status in univariable logistic regression analysis of de novo PD patients.
The same cohort of 44 Hirayama patients showed increased localized sweating in 38.6%, indicating sympathetic overactivity.
A much higher proportion of participants allocated to midodrine reported falls during 12-month follow-up compared to those allocated to fludrocortisone.
Operative duration and length of hospital stay did not significantly differ between OLIF and MIS-TLIF groups.
Pre-existing moderate or severe valvular heart disease was independently associated with the highest hazard for ABF-associated manifestations among identified risk factors.
Older cardiac remodeling patients exhibited lower LF MESOR/amplitude and higher HFab MESOR over 24 hours compared with older controls.
Older age at diagnosis was independently associated with increased risk of developing ABF-associated manifestations.
Advanced T-category (T4) oropharyngeal cancer was independently associated with an increased risk of ABF-associated manifestations.

The direction of allosteric modulation of agonist-induced Arr-2 recruitment by DCD IgG depended on timing: simultaneous addition of DCD IgG with carbachol enhanced (positive allosteric modulation) the response by 44.9%, while preincubation of M2R with DCD IgG for up to 60 minutes before carbachol produced a time-dependent switch to inhibition (negative allosteric modulation) reaching 75.4% inhibition.

Participants with OH showed a significantly greater decrease in systolic blood pressure and a smaller increase in diastolic blood pressure across the sit-up test than those without OH, per significant group-by-time interactions.

In healthy controls, nocturnal wrist temperature was negatively associated with PSQI sleep quality scores and positively associated with daily motor activity, amplitude, and activity rhythm stability, but these associations were absent in ME/CFS patients.
People with pRBD reported significantly more gastrointestinal dysfunction symptoms (constipation, diarrhoea, bloating, abdominal pain) than controls on the COMPASS-31.

After adjusting for multiple metabolic and anthropometric covariates via ANCOVA, only BEI(RRI), BEI(RQTdiff), and QTc remained statistically significant discriminators between healthy and T2DM groups.

Left ventricular mass index was significantly greater in orthostatic BP hyperreactors (SBP rise ≥5 mmHg) than in normoreactors, but this difference was not present using higher cut-offs (≥10, ≥15, ≥20 mmHg).
An independent external validation cohort confirmed that the T/L cut-off of 0.3 accurately distinguished VVS from POTS, with accuracy 81.8%, sensitivity 87.2%, specificity 77.6% overall.
Female sex was independently associated with almost double the odds of LVDD compared with male sex, after adjustment for confounders.

Severe cardiac autonomic dysfunction, defined as SDNN < 50 ms, was independently associated with a higher risk of left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD) in patients with type 2 diabetes after adjusting for confounders.

Citing prior in-vitro work, hypocapnia was reported to decrease nitric oxide (NO) levels by 30% in cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (unchanged in astrocytes), an effect prevented by the NO donor L-arginine, suggesting a possible mechanistic link between hypocapnia, endothelial dysfunction, and vasoconstriction relevant to ME/CFS.
A higher proportion of MSA patients were treated with anti-diabetic drugs compared to controls, though insulin use did not differ.

Increased resting heart rate was significantly associated with reduced FEV1/FVC ratio in linear regression across all adjustment models, though ANOVA showed no significant difference in mean FEV1/FVC ratio between heart rate quartiles.

Compared with non-progressors, the progression-to-dementia group was older, had a higher proportion of women, fewer years of education, and a higher rate of ischemic cardiomyopathy, along with a higher incidence of OH (especially DOH).

Among Black males only, multiple significant correlations emerged between catecholamines and HRV indices (HR positively with epinephrine and norepinephrine; LF-HRV, HF-HRV, and rMSSD negatively with norepinephrine), whereas White males showed only a single significant correlation (HR with norepinephrine), and no correlations emerged in Black or White females.
Participants with ocular symptoms reported significantly greater financial hardship, housing instability, and social isolation than those without ocular symptoms.
Normal supine noradrenaline, low OIR-tilt, male sex, and older age at first assessment independently predicted a final diagnosis of LBD rather than PAF.

Hospitalized test-confirmed participants had greater orthostatic intolerance (OHQ) and fatigue (FSS) burden and worse quality of life (RAND-36 subdomains) than non-hospitalized participants, despite no difference in COMPASS-31.
Multivariable logistic regression showed that AF patients, especially those in AF at recording, had substantially higher odds of cardiac autonomic dysfunction than sinus rhythm patients.
Abnormal blood pressure response to the Valsalva maneuver was found in 66% of patients at inclusion and 62% at follow-up, with no significant change over time.

Within the POTS-only (without hEDS/EDS) group, the proportion of patients with any disorganized bundles differed significantly from those with fully parallel bundles, though complete disorganization versus partly-parallel bundles did not reach significance.

Baseline MD values in the descending and ascending spinal tracts at the cervicothoracic junction significantly predicted 5-year longitudinal changes (worsening) in systolic blood pressure drop in the PDRBD(+) subgroup.

Multiple linear regression identified DHI score as an independent predictor of reduced SDNN after adjusting for age, HAMD, and QTc interval, with each 1-point increase in DHI associated with a 0.034 ms decrease in SDNN.

16% (82 individuals) of hEDS patients reported having had their symptoms dismissed as psychosomatic, which the authors note may contribute to delayed diagnosis, unnecessary antipsychotic prescription, and lasting trauma.
Mental and behavioral disorders (ICD-10 F00-F99) were significantly more prevalent in MSA patients than in non-ND controls.
For the right vagus nerve, none of the tested moderators (age, BMI, DM duration, measurement site, diagnostic criteria, study quality) significantly explained the high between-study heterogeneity.
Circulating neopterin showed a moderate inverse correlation with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), which remained significant after adjustment for age.
In female infection-triggered ME/CFS, sCD26 correlated positively with organ enzyme markers LDH, creatine kinase, ALT, AST and GGT.
Across all study participants (POTS and controls combined), lower GH levels were significantly associated with higher supine systolic blood pressure.
Apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) during NREM sleep decreased after MIH, indicating reduced sleep apnea severity.
Within the POTS subgroup alone, lower GH levels remained significantly associated with higher supine systolic blood pressure.
hESC values differed significantly across systolic BP scoring subgroups, being lower in patients with moderate or severe orthostatic intolerance compared to those without hypotension.
Compared to healthy controls, participants with chronic stroke showed a significantly greater decline in estimated failure load of the paretic distal radius over the 2-year follow-up period.
Among 101 ME patients undergoing repeated 10-min standing tests, 40 (40%) exhibited POTS during at least one test, and these patients were significantly younger than those without POTS.

Malnutrition status was significantly associated with blood pressure dipping pattern classification (dipper/non-dipper/reverse-dipper), with the reverse-dipper pattern occurring less often than expected in non-malnourished patients.

The patient's supine heart rate increase after starting tirzepatide (27 beats/min) was reported to be about 9 times greater than the average heart rate increase (3 beats/min) previously reported during the first 12 weeks of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in the general population, suggesting POTS patients may have amplified cardiovascular sensitivity to these drugs.
When comparing unselected POTS patients to healthy controls as a whole group, standard Valsalva-derived sympathetic markers were not different.
The expiration-to-inspiration (E/I) ratio during deep breathing significantly correlated with serum inflammatory markers.
Blood pressure response to sustained isometric handgrip significantly correlated with serum inflammatory markers.
The Valsalva ratio significantly correlated with serum inflammatory markers.
In treated patients only, those with two mild pathogenic GBA1 variants had lower risk of PD (HR 0.54) and 57% lower risk of pPS (HR 0.43) than those with one mild variant.
Lower MRC sum score (muscle strength) at hospitalization was independently associated with higher (worse) disability scores at last follow-up.
A prior small PET study found lower striatal 18F-DOPA influx in fibromyalgia patients compared with healthy controls, yielding a large effect size used to power the current trial.

The left PCG showed a significant negative correlation between HF and alpha-high gamma coupling before stimulation, which disappeared after stimulation, while the right PCG developed a significant positive correlation after stimulation.

Emotional functioning score was negatively correlated with orthostatic symptoms, headache, and depression scores, and physical functioning score was negatively correlated with fatigue and Nijmegen (hyperventilation) scores.
The need for mechanical ventilation was independently associated with higher (worse) disability scores at last follow-up.
Older age was independently associated with higher (worse) GBS-DS disability scores at last follow-up.

Depression and anxiety scores were correlated with fatigue domains only in healthy controls, not in ME/CFS or PCC patients, arguing against a psychological/depressive basis for fatigue in these conditions.
ME/CFS participants with COMPASS-31 orthostatic intolerance risk had significantly greater fatigue, sleep impairment, and reduced physical/social functioning than those without OI risk.
In multivariate logistic regression controlling for confounders, P wave dispersion was an independent predictor of PCPOT.
Within the RTT-F subgroup and the combined RTT groups, verticalization time was significantly positively correlated with recovery of consciousness, but not within the RTT+F or CPT subgroups alone.

Patients with a standing SBP drop rate ≥15% and/or DBP drop rate ≥5% within 3 minutes of standing (BPdrop_rate_high group) had a significantly higher risk of mortality than those in the BPdrop_rate_normal group.
Memory impairment was independently associated with higher UPDRS-III motor score, higher HY stage, and higher depression score in adjusted logistic regression.
Water intake significantly reduced overall symptoms and difficulty concentrating during head-up tilt in POTS patients but had no effect in healthy controls.

In a sensitivity analysis restricted to 129 patients with an abnormal tilt table test, hives remained significantly associated with higher Malmö POTS scores, COMPASS-31 vasomotor and urinary scores, and a trend toward higher GI scores, as well as with pain and tingling.
Eleven symbolic HR transition motifs showed significantly higher prevalence during daytime compared to nocturnal sleep.

Acute hyperoxia (to inhibit peripheral chemoreceptors) reduced ventilation and MSNA similarly in POTS and control subjects, indicating peripheral chemoreceptor activity is not exaggerated in POTS and is not a major driver of postural hyperventilation.
